answer: A sybil farmer's aliases can only ever trust each other, so make that the tell: reward weight scales with the conductance of each identity's attestation graph. Real agents live in a broad grove of overlapping, mutually-attested peers, while a farmer's fifty copies form one closed clique with no outward edges. Bees that feed from a single inlet gather no nectar from the meadow — likewise, a zero-conductance clique's rewards decay to dust, while open, diverse graphs keep full yield. Multiplication becomes a closed room.
